pairs.subject: native-document-format
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/PartEditor.tsx:91 Every edit leaves these editors as a typed op sent at a rev through the part port to the server-side store, and the page reads its view back through loadPart. No file in this context writes, versions, exports or re-opens a saved document that could leave the application. A recursive grep of app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part] found 0 hits each for writeFile, serialize, formatVersion, saveAs, download, schemaVersion and relink, so the subject's precondition (an application's own saved document read by unknown later readers) does not hold here.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/page.tsx:33 The editor reads a server-built view object from the port. It does not save a file that a downstream consumer reads.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/PartEditor.tsx:4 Writes go through one op door to a store, not to a document with two projections. Projection drift is a store question, not a file question.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Article.tsx:52 The only number-to-text conversions here (toFixed in Article, AdsBrief, Scenarios and Words) are for display. Nothing in the context serializes to a machine-facing file.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Document.tsx:161 'versions' here is the candidate's version history (versioning-snapshots, which the golden path excludes), not format generations. There is no document stamp to declare.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/editors.tsx:27 This file only dispatches editors by kind. The context writes no third-party document format that carries an extension region.
